I am 73 this year, and I have farmed in this village of Quzhou County my whole life. I only went to primary school, so I don't read those agricultural newspapers, but I know my land and I watch what my neighbors do. I have 5 mu of good flat land that I farm with my son's help.

This year, like every year, I will grow winter wheat and summer maize on the same 5 mu. That is what works here. Wheat gets planted in early October after we rotary till the soil. I use Jimai 22 seed — it is an improved variety that my neighbor Lao Zhang has used for years, and it gives steady harvests. I buy new seed every year; saving my own seed is too risky. For fertilizer, I put down about 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu before sowing, and then I topdress urea twice — once when the wheat turns green and again at jointing. In total that comes to about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu. I know some young people say that is too much, but last year I tried cutting back and the wheat turned yellow, so I went back to my old amount. Better to spend a bit more on fertilizer than to lose yield.

I irrigate four times for wheat: winter irrigation, green-up, jointing, and grain filling. The water costs money, but you cannot skip it — the rain is never enough here. For pests, I spray three times: herbicide once, and insecticide twice when I see aphids.

After wheat harvest in early June, we have no time to waste. We plant maize the same week, no-tillage, using Denghai 605 hybrid seed. Everyone uses it because it grows fast and strong. I put compound fertilizer in the hole at planting, about 80 jin per mu, and then topdress urea at the big trumpet stage. That is about 16 kg nitrogen per mu total. I irrigate twice for maize if the rain does not come — once when it is shooting up, and once during grain filling. Two pesticide sprays: herbicide and one for corn borer.

I expect about 450 kg per mu from wheat and 500 kg per mu from maize. If the weather is good, maybe a little more. I don't grow cotton anymore — my back cannot handle the picking. Wheat and maize are simple, the machines can harvest them, and the grain station buys them every year. That is enough for me at my age.
